Christmas Pudding

Served at: Christmas Day

Serves 8Prep 30 minCook 8 hours (steaming)

Christmas Pudding is a traditional British dessert served on Christmas Day, known for its rich, dense texture and deep flavors from dried fruits, spices, and suet. It is often prepared weeks in advance to allow the flavors to mature, and it is traditionally steamed and served with brandy butter or cream.

Ingredients

  • 1 cup (150 g) currants
  • 1 cup (150 g) raisins
  • 1 cup (150 g) sultanas
  • 1/2 cup (75 g) chopped dried figs
  • 1/2 cup (75 g) chopped dried dates
  • 1/2 cup (75 g) chopped candied peel
  • 1/2 cup (120 ml) dark stout or ale
  • 1/4 cup (60 ml) brandy
  • 1 cup (100 g) fresh white breadcrumbs
  • 1 cup (100 g) all-purpose flour
  • 1/2 cup (100 g) dark brown sugar, packed
  • 1/2 teaspoon ground cinnamon
  • 1/2 teaspoon ground nutmeg
  • 1/4 teaspoon ground cloves
  • 1/4 teaspoon ground ginger
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 1/2 cup (115 g) beef suet, shredded (or vegetable suet for vegetarian)
  • 3 large eggs, beaten
  • 1 small apple, peeled and grated
  • Zest of 1 lemon
  • Zest of 1 orange

Method

  1. In a large bowl, combine currants, raisins, sultanas, figs, dates, and candied peel.
  2. Pour the stout and brandy over the dried fruits, stir well, and let soak overnight or at least 4 hours.
  3. In another bowl, mix together breadcrumbs, flour, brown sugar, spices, salt, and suet.
  4. Add the soaked fruits with their liquid to the dry ingredients.
  5. Stir in the beaten eggs, grated apple, lemon zest, and orange zest until fully combined.
  6. Grease a 2-quart (2-liter) pudding basin and spoon the mixture into it, pressing down lightly.
  7. Cover the basin with a layer of parchment paper and a layer of foil, securing tightly with string.
  8. Place the pudding basin in a large pot with a trivet or folded towel at the bottom to prevent burning.
  9. Pour boiling water into the pot to come halfway up the sides of the basin.
  10. Cover the pot with a lid and steam the pudding for 6 to 8 hours, checking the water level and topping up with boiling water as needed.
  11. Remove the pudding from the pot and let cool completely. Store in a cool, dry place until Christmas Day.
  12. To serve, steam the pudding again for 2 hours to reheat.
  13. Turn out onto a serving plate, flame with warmed brandy if desired, and serve with brandy butter or cream.

Tips

  • Prepare the pudding at least 4 weeks in advance to allow the flavors to mature and develop.
  • Use a clean cotton cloth instead of parchment and foil for a more traditional steaming method.
  • For a vegetarian version, substitute beef suet with vegetable suet or grated cold butter.
